n: An invitation to worship: come, sing, and shout for joy to the Lord, the solid ‘rock’ who saves us. This psalm became a traditional call to worship in Jewish and Christian services.

f.g: A loud shout of praise, like the cheer for a king.

n: Approach God with thanks and songs. Gratitude is the doorway into his presence.
The reason for praise: the Lord is the great King, far above every so-called god of the nations.
From the deepest depths of the earth to the highest mountain peaks, everything is in God’s hand.
Sea and land both belong to God because he made them. Creation is the basis of his kingship.

f.w: his hands formed the dry land

n: A second invitation: bow down and kneel before our Maker. Worship involves the body as well as the heart.
We are God’s flock, cared for by his own hand. Then the tone shifts sharply: ‘Today, if you will hear his voice…’

f.w: To day if ye will hear his voice

n: Now God speaks: don’t be stubborn like Israel in the wilderness. ‘Provocation’ (Meribah) and ‘temptation’ (Massah) are the place names where Israel quarreled with God over water.
The Israelites put God to the test and challenged him — even though they had seen his miracles.
For forty years God was grieved by that generation, whose hearts kept wandering and who never truly learned his ways.
So God declared they would not enter his ‘rest’ — the promised land. Hebrews and the D&C apply this ‘rest’ to entering the fulness of God’s glory.
